CSA design-system implementation notes
Current approved behavior · 2026-10-26

2026-10-23: Homepage greeting, grid cards, and list rows use a whole-element fade and upward glide together: opacity 0 to 1, 40px starting offset, 300ms duration, symmetric ease-in-out, and no delay or stagger. Component layout home-enter tokens define these values; the 300ms cleanup matches the entrance duration. Home-entry replay remains available, and reduced motion shows the greeting, grid cards, and list rows immediately.

2026-10-23: Text-field and unchecked-checkbox outlines use semantic.color.border.control (Neutral 500, #737373), aliased by component.field.border and component.checkbox.border. Boundary contrast is 4.74:1 on white, 4.66:1 on the current Amber 50 at 50% over white (#FFFDF5) canvas, and 4.35:1 on Neutral 100, meeting the 3:1 non-text minimum. The DS includes editable-field and unchecked-checkbox examples. Neutral 200 stays on decorative card/panel/divider borders and dropdown outlines with dark labels and chevrons. Checked controls use Teal 700 (#00786F) fills and white checks; selected borders and keyboard-focus outlines use the same teal accent. Reference color roles document both uses without duplicate swatches.

2026-10-23: Homepage contrast colors: project dates, generated-content counts, and enabled project-menu ellipsis icons use semantic.color.text.secondary (Neutral 500, #737373). Contrast is 4.74:1 on white, meeting the 4.5:1 normal-text and 3:1 essential-icon minimums. Supporting text directly on the Amber 50 at 50% over white (#FFFDF5) canvas uses semantic.color.text.canvas-secondary (#404040) at 10.18:1; Neutral 500 is 4.66:1 on that canvas and remains suitable there for essential icons and boundaries. The selected layout uses component.layout-switch.selected-background (Teal 700, #00786F) and selected-label (inverse white), with 5.36:1 contrast. Neutral 200 remains appropriate for decorative card and divider borders when readable text or icons identify the controls; visible keyboard-focus indicators are still required. The color-role gallery and isolated homepage specimens document these approved colors.

2026-10-23: Approved palette roles: the page canvas, editor footer, and source-card Publish Date/URL footer use Amber 50 at 50% over white (#FFFDF5). Structural navigation/sidebar, New Draft, Content, editor, and source panels use white. Inner card bodies, including source titles and snippets, fields, menus, and dialogs use white; source metadata footers have a thin top divider. Headings remain near-black (#060606), body text remains dark gray (#404040), and supporting text on white remains Neutral 500 (#737373). Primary actions, links, selected labels and borders, checked fills, and focus indicators now use Teal 700 (#00786F); hover or pressed accents use Teal 800 (#005F5A), and soft selected surfaces use Teal 50 (#F0FDFA). Primary white-label contrast is 5.36:1 by default and 7.54:1 on hover. Disabled fills and labels remain neutral. Secondary actions retain white surfaces with teal text and outlines. Tertiary actions retain borderless text styling and a neutral hover fill. Selected joined editor tabs match the white panel; content cards remain white, with teal labels or indicators. Format Rose 200, Audience Indigo 100, and Voice Orange 200 chips, green Sent status, and red destructive states retain their roles. Canvas fades use #FFFDF5 at 230/255 opacity (#FFFDF5E6).

2026-10-23: Draft status tabs match the Content panel: Content to Draft / Drafted labels, Inter Medium (500), a 16 px gap, light-gray full-width baseline, and a 2 px teal active underline. Labels and underline transition over 200 ms; reduced motion switches immediately. The DS specimen and app use the same shared component rules.

2026-10-23: To Draft, Draft, and Sent status badge labels match settings chips: Inter Medium (500), 12 px with a 20 px line height. semantic.typography.status aliases semantic.typography.chip so both stay aligned.

2026-10-23: Format, Audience, and Voice dropdown values use Inter Regular (400). The shared dropdown field-value role and panel dropdown triggers use the same semantic weight token.

2026-10-23: Project grid-card headings use Inter Semibold (600), 16 px with a 20 px line height on desktop and mobile. The DS specimens and local homepage share the project-title role.

2026-10-23: Approved typography consolidation uses six shared text sizes: 12, 14, 16, 20, 24, and 30 px. Choose sizes by role instead of retaining near-duplicate component exceptions: metadata 12/16 and status/chips 12/20; project grid-card titles 16/20; list titles, labels, and regular dropdown values 14/20; text inputs and secondary actions 16/24; primary action labels 16/20; body text 16/28; New Draft and Content headings 16/24; other panel headings 20/28; dialog headings 24/32 at weight 650 with zero tracking; article section headings 24/32; desktop greeting and editor title 30/36, with compact/mobile titles 24/32. Project grid-card headings and secondary action labels use Semibold (600); status and chip labels use Medium (500), and dropdown values remain Regular (400). Material Symbols use a separate foundation.icon.size scale of 16, 20, 24, and 40 px, with glyph boxes matched to the selected size. Exported documents share 16/28 body text and 30/36, 24/32, and 20/28 heading levels.

2026-10-23: Approved font families: Newsreader remains the serif homepage greeting and optional serif article style; Inter is the interface family for controls, navigation, cards, headings, and standard reading text. Typography roles retain the approved sizes, weights, and line heights. Material Symbols Outlined remains the icon font, and system monospace remains available for code.

2026-10-23: Removed unused reference colors from the DS token inventory and color gallery: previous Blue 50/200/500/600/700, Orange 50 canvas source, warm canvas and fade, and the legacy #26344A editor color-input default. The hidden browser color picker now initializes from the existing Neutral 700 (#404040) body color. The heading color (#060606), backdrop, and functional chip/status/destructive colors remain in use; the old black primary and #454545 hover tokens were retired when teal accents were introduced.

2026-10-23: Empty Format, Audience, and Voice dropdown triggers show their purpose as the placeholder. None Selected remains an option in each menu for clearing the value; clearing restores the Format, Audience, or Voice trigger label. This behavior is shared by the app and DS selection/disclosure specimens.

2026-10-23: Toast Undo actions use the filled Material Symbols undo icon instead of visible Undo text, with aria-label and title set to Undo. The icon is included in the DS inventory and loaded font subset; the Source Image/photo_camera icon has been removed from the DS gallery. The app-only legacy result-thumbnail glyph remains in its own font subset. Existing undo callbacks and 9-second action timing are preserved.

2026-10-23: Content to Draft cards no longer display a separate selection checkbox. The main card button toggles pending selection and exposes aria-pressed, while the teal selected border remains visible. Source article selection checkboxes are unchanged.

2026-10-23: Editorial Direction textarea text and placeholder use Inter Regular (400), 14 px with a 20 px line height in the composer and results views on desktop and mobile. This compact component uses the shared 14/20 tokens; other text inputs retain the generic 16/24 input-value role. The DS specimen inherits the same component styling.

2026-10-23: Drafting cards retain a white background and the fixed label Drafting Content. Timed paper phases advance through selected categories in canonical Format/Audience/Voice order: pink, lavender, and peach, skipping unselected categories. One selection keeps its color, two selections alternate, and all three cycle pink → lavender → peach. With no choices, legacy content uses a neutral shimmer. component.drafting.shimmer.format, .audience, and .voice alias the corresponding chip backgrounds; component.drafting.shimmer-duration sets the 2400 ms sweep. Each visual phase holds for 5 seconds before an 800 ms paper handoff. Paper sheets stay white, shared paper lines use Neutral 500 (#737373), and the dark label does not change. Reduced motion hides the sweep and keeps a static sheet and label.

2026-10-25: The app and DS page canvas use Amber 50 (#FFFBEB) at 50% over white, flattened to opaque #FFFDF5 so overlapping canvas surfaces retain one color. foundation.color.canvas.amber-50-half supplies semantic.color.background.canvas and records the source blend recipe; the raw Amber source is not retained as an unused swatch. foundation.color.overlay.amber-canvas-fade uses resolved #FFFDF5 at 230/255 alpha (#FFFDF5E6). Supporting text directly on the canvas uses semantic.color.text.canvas-secondary, an alias of Primary text (#404040), at 10.18:1 contrast. Secondary text (#737373) measures 4.74:1 on white and 4.66:1 on the resolved canvas, meeting normal-text and essential-icon minimums. Near-black heading text (#060606) measures 19.90:1 on the canvas. White panels and inner cards retain their existing text and icon roles.

2026-10-25: The approved 60/30/10 palette uses cream canvas (#FFFDF5), white panels and inner content, and deep teal accents as a loose visual balance. Teal 700 (#00786F) supplies primary actions, links, plus icons, selected labels/borders/checked fills, and focus outlines; Teal 800 (#005F5A) supplies hover and pressed accents. Teal 50 (#F0FDFA), via semantic.color.surface.selected, supplies selected navigation and supporting selection-control tints. Recipe and WordPress destination menu rows retain neutral text and backgrounds; their selected checkmarks use teal. White labels on default/hover teal measure 5.36:1/7.54:1; default teal on cream is 5.27:1 and on Teal 50 is 5.14:1. Headings and body text retain their neutral colors; joined editor tabs match the white panel, inner cards remain white, and functional chip, Sent, and danger colors remain. Material selection controls retain outlined unselected icons and filled selected icons.

2026-10-25: New Draft and Content panel headings use Inter Bold (700), 16 px with a 24 px line height on desktop and mobile. Shared composer-panel component tokens keep app panels, DS specimens, and typography guidance aligned. Their icons remain 20 px; other panel-heading roles remain 20 px.

2026-10-25: Source result-card Publish Date and URL metadata form a cream footer matching the editor footer: semantic.color.background.canvas (#FFFDF5) with a thin Neutral 200 top divider. The source-card title and snippet body remain white. The card outline, rounded corners, and selection behavior are preserved.

2026-10-25: Format, Audience, and Voice dropdown triggers use the Material Symbols unfold_less icon in the app and DS. The icon stays static in open and closed states; the trigger exposes the actual expanded state through aria-expanded. The icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Panel disclosure controls retain their existing keyboard_arrow_up/keyboard_arrow_down collapse and expand icons.

2026-10-25: Outer workspace panel gutters and the New Draft/Content panel gap use 16 px through shared aliases of foundation.space.16. Desktop keeps 16 px at the top, right, bottom, and navigation left edge. Mobile keeps a 16 px outer top-bar gutter and 16 px left/right/bottom main-content insets. The 64 px top bar plus its outer gutter and 16 px following gap place main content and open panels at 96 px; open panels have 16 px side insets and at least 16 px bottom clearance, using a 112 px height budget. DS state-panel examples use the same 16 px gap. Card and control inner padding is unchanged.

2026-10-25: Drafting cards pass selected recipe categories through createDraftingAnimation({ selectionKeys }). data-shimmer-colors lists the allowed categories in canonical format/audience/voice order; data-shimmer-color exposes the single active category for the current visual phase. data-phase-index and data-phase-count expose paper-cycle state. The DS shows Format only, Audience + Voice, and all three categories selected, with visible labels; only the first repeated static label is announced live. Each preview preserves the shared paper handoff, fixed dark Drafting Content label, and controller cleanup. Source adding keeps its fixed Teal 50 shimmer.

2026-10-25: The Drafting Content label is left-aligned in the shared app and DS drafting component; the source-adding variant keeps its centered label.

2026-10-25: Drafting previews refresh their visible bounds on scroll, resize, and page visibility changes rather than relying solely on cached IntersectionObserver state. Visible DS cards resume automatically; clipped/offscreen cards, hidden pages, and reduced motion remain paused.

2026-10-25: Adding a source uses createSourceAddingAnimation(): a white card with one centered paper above the centered text Adding your Source. Its fixed Teal 50 (#F0FDFA) shimmer shares the 2400 ms loading sweep, and its paper lines use Neutral 500 (#737373). The source variant keeps its fixed label and has no paper handoff; reduced motion hides the sweep and keeps the paper and text static. The DS replaces its former spinner/Adding example with the same shared controller and destroys it when the specimen unmounts.

2026-10-25: Source headline hover uses the shared gray surface with 8 px corners; keyboard focus keeps its outline. Selected recipe dropdown options and WordPress destinations keep neutral text and row backgrounds, with a teal checkmark indicating selection. Pointer hover remains gray and keyboard-focus outlines remain visible.

2026-10-25: Homepage list rows share the grid-card entrance: 300 ms, ease-in-out, 40 px upward glide, with no delay or stagger and immediate display for reduced motion. List rows retain their ordinary neutral dividers, white fill, dark text, and unchanged geometry. Hover adds subtle elevation; row controls keep visible keyboard-focus outlines. Project deletion dialogs in the app and DS omit the extra warning paragraph.

2026-10-25: Editor tab titles use Inter at 14 px with a 24 px line height; active titles remain Semibold (600), and inactive titles remain Regular (400).

2026-10-26: Structural navigation/sidebar, New Draft, Content, editor, and source panels return to white. semantic.color.surface.panel aliases the shared white foundation color; the selected joined editor tab matches it. Inner cards, fields, menus, and dialogs stay white, while the cream canvas and footers remain unchanged. Project grid-card headings remain Inter Semibold (600), 16 px with a 20 px line height on desktop and mobile; homepage list titles and editor-tab titles retain 14 px. Format chips now use Rose 200, Audience chips Indigo 100, and Voice chips Orange 200. Drafting shimmer steps use these same selected-category colors; editor text highlight retains Orange 100.

2026-10-26: Content status tabs and project layout switches use the same selection controllers in the app and DS. Content status uses tablist/tab/tabpanel semantics, aria-selected, roving tabindex, and Arrow/Home/End navigation; project layout retains grouped aria-pressed buttons with its existing Tab stops and the same arrow navigation. The DS list toolbar includes the shared New Project action. Specimens use isolated data and callbacks without reading saved projects.

2026-10-26: Source media and container queries use token(foundation.breakpoint.name). The design-system build resolves those thresholds to literals in generated CSS; generated exports remain read-only.

2026-10-26: The editor footer separates visible word count, save status, Created timestamp, and Editorial Direction metadata with decorative dots. Hidden fields do not leave extra separators; each dot stays attached to the following item when metadata wraps. The cream footer surface and top divider remain shared.

2026-10-26: Article titles in the Project Sources panel use Inter Regular (400), 14 px with a 20 px line height. semantic.typography.source-title aliases the shared field-value role; the source title hover and focus treatments remain unchanged.

2026-10-26: The sidebar navigation item, tooltip, and source panel use the name Project Sources. Source counts, draft-specific source actions, the folder_open glyph, and internal identifiers retain their existing names.

2026-10-26: A draft’s source-count chip opens the shared anchored Sources Used popover. Its heading is Source Used for one source and Sources Used for zero or multiple sources; source-count chip labels use Source or Sources. It sits 8 px below the visible chip; its folder heading, full regular-weight source titles, and close button match the current reference. It lists only that draft’s saved source snapshots. Selecting a title closes the popover and opens the same createSourcePreview modal used by the sidebar, with the captured source content. The separate Project Sources sidebar stays closed and source selections remain unchanged. The DS uses two isolated link/text snapshots with captured paragraphs, plus an unused project source, to demonstrate the boundary without accessing saved browser data.

2026-10-26: Project Sources rows use label.editor-source-selection around a native input.editor-source-checkbox. The shared checkbox has a 44 px target and a 24 px visual control, with an accessible Use source for new drafts label. The checkboxes automatically follow the active draft’s exact captured source set when editor tabs change; the initial counter says used in this draft. Editing a checkbox applies a next-draft selection and changes the counter to selected for new drafts, without rewriting existing article text or source snapshots. New drafts capture only checked sources. The isolated DS example switches between a saved two-source draft and a saved one-source draft; the one-source example checks the second row to demonstrate exact set matching. Title preview remains separate from checkbox selection through the shared read-only source preview.

2026-10-26: Content cards and compact drafting cards share component.variant-card.min-height (90 px) and the 8 px variant-card radius. Loading outlines use the normal 1 px variant-card border width in Neutral 200 (#E5E5E5), including while an active card is processing. Compact drafting uses 12 px padding; revision overlays preserve the existing outer footprint, retaining a selected card’s 92 px height even with the 1 px loading outline. DS drafting previews use the same 320 px maximum width as the content-card specimen. The standalone source-adding preview retains its separate compact 120 px minimum and centered single-page layout; embedded source-adding overlays continue to fill their parent.

2026-10-27: Metadata is the first editor-footer action and opens the current draft’s derived SEO title, meta description, and SEO keywords. Requested Revision (one) or Requested Revisions (multiple) appears last after completion. Its anchored popup retains every request in chronological order with its completion timestamp and full requested change. Revision completion preserves the current tab and marks the revised draft with an 8 px #B91C1C unread dot; activating that tab clears the dot. Dot-to-title spacing is 8 px.

2026-10-27: Revising Draft covers the settings, title, subhead, toolbar, and full body area at their existing inset, preserving document geometry and using 8 px corners. Send to CMS stays outside the loading area. Selected Format/Audience/Voice shimmer colors follow the same canonical order as drafting and fit into the 5-second revision preview. Inactive revising tabs show the same category animation with a compact paper stack and Revising Draft label. All loading labels now use Inter Medium Italic (500). Adding Source replaces Adding your Source and sits beside its single paper; the fixed mint shimmer and reduced-motion behavior remain shared.

2026-10-27: App and DS toast behavior now uses one controller and shared duration tokens: 5 seconds for message-only toasts and 10 seconds for Undo. New notifications replace the previous timer and action; Undo is consumed once before its callback runs. Microcopy uses short sentence-case outcomes, consistent source/draft/project nouns, no final period, and useful recovery instructions for errors. Toasts fit their content up to 440 px with equal 16 px horizontal padding. The DS previews the shared timers and documents the wording rules.

2026-10-28: Completed-revision dots remain 8 px and #B91C1C. When the revised draft stays selected, its dot clears after 10 seconds through component.editor-tab.revision-dot-active-duration, without changing the selected tab or editor content. Switching away cancels the timer, so unread dots on other tabs stay until those tabs are activated. A new revision starts a fresh completion interval; repeated renders do not extend it. Automatic acknowledgement is persisted in the app and shared by the DS preview. Leaving the editor suspends its timer.

2026-10-28: Collapsed New Draft panels use component.composer-panel.collapsed-padding-block (12 px) equally above and below their header on desktop and mobile. Expanded panel spacing is preserved. The app and DS use the same collapsed-state selector and component token.

2026-10-28: Content now shares the New Draft heading disclosure: a full-width clickable title with a right chevron, 200 ms measured-height animation, reduced-motion handling, and accessible expanded/hidden/inert states. Its status tabs, cards, and footer close together, while their selections and data are retained. The app saves contentCollapsed per project. Collapsed Content uses the shared 12 px block-padding token and drops the expanded minimum height; expanded Content keeps its scrollable flex layout. The DS previews the same controller and styling.
